items.title: Bill Ackman Says the Fed Is “About to Make Another Mistake” on Dec. 9
items.summary: Bill Ackman wants the Fed to abandon its 2% inflation goal before a rate decision that markets already expect. His case rests on one startling borrowing cost, and the Fed chair has already shut the door on his idea.

items.title: Smith + Nephew names new CFO
items.summary: Nick Alexos will join the orthopedics company later this month after holding CFO roles at Univar Solutions and Dentsply Sirona.

items.title: Jensen Huang back at Nvidia, stock soars; Anthropic slides
items.summary: The 8:30 team is joined by Roundhill Investments Chief Investment Strategist Drew Pettit to discuss why washed-out sentiment doesn't mean a fundamental bottom, his $50-to-$250 bull-bear range on Anthropic, and how to handicap the "Jensen premium" coming back into Nvidia. Deirdre Bosa Live host Deirdre Bosa also joins to break down Silicon Valley's reaction to Huang's return and what it means for the AI trade.

items.title: Victory Capital Holdings (VCTR) Partners With Apollo, Is It Still A Bargain?
items.summary: Victory Capital Holdings (VCTR) just moved to deepen its product lineup, announcing a collaboration with Apollo Global Management that combines Apollo’s private markets expertise with Victory’s public markets and distribution reach. Recent trading has been choppy for Victory Capital Holdings, with the share price down 11.9% over the past week and 3.4% on the day. items.title: SpaceX Is Paying Up to 8.36% on $44 Billion of Debt for Nvidia Chips
items.summary: Lenders lined up to fund SpaceX's chip spree, then demanded a steep price for it. The real risk may be what happens to those GPUs, and to SpaceX's cash flow, before the first rent check clears.

items.title: Apollo (APO) Stock May Be 30% Undervalued As AI Credit Risks Loom
items.summary: Apollo Global Management has delivered a 70.4% total return over the past 5 years, yet the recent share price pullback and fresh deal activity put a sharper spotlight on whether that valuation can be explained by the returns it earns on its capital. A 70.4% gain over 5 years puts real weight on the question of whether Apollo's current price is anchored in the actual profitability of the capital it deploys for clients and on its own balance sheet.
